title: Effective Risk
description: The Air Force’s history is a timeline rich in success stories of innovation and calculated risks taken by Airmen to achieve a legacy of dominance in airpower, yet behind any of these success stories there’s a series of lessons learned from failure.
keywords: risk, crash, space, Senior Leaders, innovation, failure, General John E. Hyten, Lt Gen Steven L. Kwast, failing, Heather Wilson, Dr. Roper, Thunderbirds Ejections, history

transcript.text: - [Narrator] There were a number of failures during the year
and the United States promptly announced them.
- Admiral Rickover, the father of nuclear navy,
he had a classic line, "We learn nothing from success,
"we only learn from failure."
(shouting)
(single beep)
- [Man] God dammit.
- I don't think our people are
in a place where they're afraid to fail.
But I think the system that we're operating in
is afraid to fail, and that's a dangerous thing.
(garbled talk over radio)
- I've had a lot of failures in the past.
I was fortunate that I was able to have
those failures in a way that wasn't catastrophic.
And I'm not sure that I would be in this job.
But one event that I think about a lot is that I realize
I'm the beneficiary of a double standard.
That we like to talk about risk taking
but we only reward the people for whom that risk works out.
And that's not the way that we should do it.
A good risk is a good risk regardless of the outcome.
- I just want us all to remember
that we all play a part in this legacy.
(clapping)
- Because one of the key elements
of innovation is the ability to take risk,
one of the key elements of innovation
is creating an environment where people
are free to speak things that might be considered heresy.
But it is truth, and it is exploring
new ways to solve old problems.
- The Air force can be a little bit top down sometimes.
And a little bit dependent on Air force instructions,
and we want to get away from that,
so that we tell people what to do and not how to do it,
and let them surprise us with there ingenuity.
(intense music)
